user.title: Tuya account
user.description: Sign in with the account the cameras belong to. Every device on it is probed once, and the ones that answer the IPC config API are imported as cameras.

data_description.country_code: The calling code of the account's country, without a plus sign — 1 for the US, 55 for Brazil.
data_description.region: The Tuya data centre the account lives in.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in again
reauth_confirm.description: The Tuya cloud rejected the stored credentials. The cameras already configured are kept.

reconfigure.title: Tuya account
reconfigure.description: Update the account and refresh the list of cameras it exposes.

error.auth: The email, password, country code or region is wrong.
error.connection: Could not reach the Tuya cloud.
error.no_cameras: No device on this account answers the IPC config API, so there is nothing to stream.

abort.unique_id_mismatch: The credentials belong to a different account.

data_description.keep_connected: Hold the camera session open so video and snapshots are ready instantly. These cameras serve one client at a time, so while this is on the Tuya app cannot connect to them. Turn it off to share a camera: the session then comes up on demand and is released a minute after the last viewer leaves.
data_description.motion_sensitivity: How much a frame has to differ from the one before it to count as motion, as a multiple of the difference this camera shows when nothing is happening. Lower catches more and reports more false alarms.
data_description.scan_interval: How often the account is polled for camera names, availability and rotated local keys. It does not affect the video, which is pushed.

needs_power_cycle.title: {camera} has stopped answering and needs to be power cycled
needs_power_cycle.description: `{camera}` is turning down every connection with its "busy" reply, which these cameras do after a run of failed attempts and keep doing for every client — the Tuya app cannot load the picture either. Nothing Home Assistant can do clears it: unplug the camera for a few seconds and plug it back in. Home Assistant is now retrying it slowly, and this notice disappears on its own once the camera streams again.
